iOS 27 introduces several improvements for Apple Pay, including a fully overhauled checkout flow that’s the service’s best upgrade in years.

New design for Apple Pay checkout screen in iOS 27 is better in every way

Apple Pay has become one of the most popular payment methods in the world. It’s so universally available that even Walmart finally gave in and added support.

And with its popularity, any significant change Apple implements could be risky—especially a design change like iOS 27 brings.

Apple Pay has a new design in iOS 27 when checking out in apps or on the web. And I’m happy to report it’s a fantastic upgrade that’s better in every way.

The old checkout design had a couple main faults:

  • Switching cards wasn’t intuitive
  • Onscreen data wasn’t easy to parse at a glance

Despite years of using Apple Pay, I’ve still never gotten used to the historic method for switching cards. I always tap near the top where the active card is displayed, only to load the address screen and have to go back to find the actual card selection menu.

iOS 27 fixes that. When you first open the checkout interface, you’ll see additional cards on either side of your default card, indicating you can swipe between them to switch. It’s quick, easy, and far more intuitive.

Additionally, iOS 27 shows more information onscreen at once, and uses colorful icons to denote relevant info like shipping method and address, billing address, and more.

The redesign makes it much easier to verify everything is accurate and as it should be. Then you can quickly double click to pay with the assurance there are no mistakes.

Changing the design for something used by millions, and with real-world consequences for errors, is a tall task. But in my opinion, Apple has done a fantastic job with iOS 27’s Apple Pay revamp.

What do you think of the new Apple Pay checkout design in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
